title: EA-CORPORA-30 — The Thirtieth Seating: The Exact Sciences — Einstein, Gödel, Tesla, Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler, Newton, Classical Arabic Mathematics, the Found
sentence: Heiberg (1907): found on the Archive (claudiiptolemae04ptolgoog, claudiiptolemae05ptolgoog) and held back as outside the Syntaxis asked for; Ptolemy, Apotelesmatica (Tetrabiblos): the Perseus text is Robbins's Loeb (1940) and the First1KGreek text is Boll and Boer (1954); held back, both printed after 1930 - Cross-references: in_this_library: Euclid in Heiberg's Greek (data/corpora/euclid, EA-CORPORA-20/04); the Arabic Almagest of Isḥāq ibn Ḥunayn revised by Thābit ibn Qurra, Thābit's Tashīl al-Majisṭī and his Arabic Apollonius (arabic-mathematics, 30/08); Copernicus (30/04) and Kepler (30/06) in this seating. - Why seated: Archimedes and Ptolemy are the two Greek authors whose demonstrations the Arabic and Latin traditions carried longest: the Sphere and Cylinder and the Sand-Reckoner on one side, the Syntaxis on the other, which the Arabs called al-Majisṭī.
